q: Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways; the ____ and the vector product.
e: Vectors can be multiplied to yield either a scalar (dot product) or a vector (cross product).

q: In the scalar product, a ____ can be formed by multiplying two vectors.
e: The dot product of two vectors results in a scalar quantity, not a vector.

q: The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as Eq. (2.1), ____.
e: The scalar product is calculated by multiplying the magnitudes of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle between them.

q: The scalar product is also called the ____.
e: Because the operator used is a dot ($\cdot$), the scalar product is commonly referred to as the dot product.

q: For example, ____ is the scalar product of force and displacement.
e: Work is a scalar quantity derived from the dot product of the vector quantities force and displacement.

q: The scalar product has the ____ property as described by Eq.(2.2) $A \cdot B = B \cdot A$.
e: The order of vectors in a scalar product does not change the result, making it commutative.

q: The vector product of vectors A and B is defined as ____.
e: The cross product of two vectors results in a new vector quantity C.

q: The magnitude of C is $C = AB \sin \theta$ and the direction of C is determined by using the ____.
e: The right-hand rule is used to find the perpendicular direction of the resulting vector in a cross product.

q: The direction of C is ____ to the plane that contains A and B.
e: The resulting vector of a cross product is always orthogonal (perpendicular) to the plane formed by the two original vectors.

q: The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross (x), hence this product is called the ____.
e: The cross symbol ($\times$) gives the vector product its alternative name.

q: The vector product does not obey the ____ property as Eq.(2.4) $A \times B = -(B \times A)$.
e: Reversing the order of vectors in a cross product reverses the direction of the resulting vector, making it anti-commutative.

q: The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the ____.
e: Torque ($\tau = r \times F$) and tangential velocity ($v = \omega \times r$) are defined using the cross product.

q: To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are ____ to thumb.
e: The fingers must be mutually perpendicular to correctly represent the three orthogonal axes of the vectors.

q: Now rotate your hand such that your index finger points in the direction of A and your ____ points in the direction of B.
e: In the right-hand rule, the index finger represents the first vector and the middle finger represents the second vector.

q: Your ____ will point in the direction of the cross product $A \times B$.
e: The thumb indicates the direction of the resultant vector C from the cross product.

q: Torque is a vector quantity and its vector form can be expressed as ____.
e: The summary reiterates that torque is defined by the cross product of the position vector and the force vector.

q: The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque is defined as the product of force and the ____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: This is the core definition of the magnitude of torque.

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the ____ in a given object and the square of its distance from the axis.
e: This summarizes the discrete particle definition of moment of inertia.

q: The angular momentum L of an object is defined as the product of its moment of inertia I and ____.
e: This is the fundamental definition of angular momentum provided in the chapter summary.

q: When a force is applied to an object, it can turn the object about a certain point known as the pivot(or) the ____.
e: The fixed point around which an object rotates when a force is applied is called the pivot or fulcrum.

q: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the ____ of that force (or) torque.
e: The moment of a force quantifies its tendency to cause rotation about a specific point.

q: Torque is a ____ quantity and its vector form can be expressed as the Eq.(2.5), $\tau = r \times F$.
e: Torque has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity defined by a cross product.

q: The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque $\tau$ is defined as the product of the force F and the ____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: Only the component of distance perpendicular to the force's line of action contributes to the torque.

q: The equation for the magnitude of torque can be written as $\tau = Fr \sin \theta =$ ____.
e: Since $d = r \sin \theta$, the torque can be simplified to the product of force and the perpendicular moment arm $d$.

q: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum ($d = r \sin \theta$) is also called the ____ of a force.
e: The moment arm is the shortest (perpendicular) distance between the axis of rotation and the line of action of the force.

q: The ____ of a force is a line along which a force is considered to act.
e: The line of action is an imaginary infinite line extending in both directions along the vector of the applied force.

q: In SI units, the moment of force (or) torque is measured in newton metre (N m), which is never written as ____.
e: Although dimensionally equivalent to the joule, the newton metre is used for torque to distinguish it from energy or work.

q: According to ____, $F = ma = mr\alpha$.
e: Newton's second law relates the tangential force on a particle to its mass and tangential acceleration ($a = r\alpha$).

q: Torque due to tangential force; $\tau = Fr = (mr\alpha)r$.
e: The torque causing angular acceleration is generated by the component of force acting tangentially to the circular path.

q: The torque equation simplifies to $\tau =$ ____.
e: Multiplying the terms gives $mr^2\alpha$, where $mr^2$ represents the rotational inertia of the particle.

q: In Eq.(2.7) the terms $mr^2$ is the ____ of that particle about the axis (I).
e: For a single particle, the moment of inertia is the product of its mass and the square of its distance from the axis.

q: The rotational equivalent of Newton's second law is written as ____.
e: This equation shows that torque is the product of moment of inertia and angular acceleration.

q: The moment of inertia of an object composed of multiple particles is $I = $ ____.
e: The total moment of inertia is the sum of the moments of inertia of all individual particles making up the object.

q: The moment of inertia I can be written in summation notation as ____.
e: The sigma notation compactly represents the sum of the products of mass and the square of the distance for all particles.

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle in a given object and the ____ from the axis.
e: Distance is squared in the moment of inertia formula, meaning mass further from the axis contributes disproportionately more to rotational inertia.

q: The moment of inertia is a ____ and the SI unit is $kg \cdot m^2$.
e: Unlike torque or angular momentum, moment of inertia has magnitude but no direction, making it a scalar quantity.

q: The moment of inertia must be specified with respect to a chosen ____.
e: An object's moment of inertia changes depending on which axis it is rotating around.

q: The ____ of a particular object is a point at which all its weight may be considered to act.
e: The centre of gravity is the average location of the weight of an object.

q: For an object of regular shape and ____, the centre of gravity is at its geometrical center.
e: Symmetry and uniform mass distribution ensure the centre of gravity aligns with the geometric center.

q: For example, the weight of a metre stick of uniform density is considered to be acting at the ____ (its mid-point).
e: The midpoint of a uniform 100 cm metre stick is at the 50 cm mark, which is its centre of gravity.

q: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its axis of rotation is ____.
e: This is the standard formula for the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere rotating about its central axis.

q: When the system is in ____, there is no linear motion and no rotational motion.
e: Static equilibrium means the object is completely at rest, with no translational or rotational acceleration.

q: Under this condition, the forces on it must be balanced and the ____ on it must also be balanced.
e: Both net force and net torque must be zero for an object to remain in static equilibrium.

q: The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the ____ on the system is zero, $\Sigma F = 0$, and (2) the resultant torque on the system is zero, $\Sigma \tau = 0$.
e: The first condition of equilibrium ensures there is no linear acceleration.

q: The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the resultant force on the system is zero, $\Sigma F = 0$, and (2) the ____ on the system is zero, $\Sigma \tau = 0$.
e: The second condition of equilibrium ensures there is no angular acceleration.

q: The condition necessary for a pivoted object to be in balance is given by the ____.
e: The principle of moments is the foundational rule for solving static equilibrium problems involving pivots.

q: This principle states that if an object such as a bar (or) a plank is to be in balance, the total ____ about the fulcrum must equal the total anticlockwise moment.
e: For rotational equilibrium, the sum of torques trying to rotate the object clockwise must exactly cancel those trying to rotate it anticlockwise.

q: The examples of the application of this principle are building site crane, ____ etc.
e: A beam balance uses the principle of moments to compare unknown masses with known standard masses.

q: In rotational motion, the angular momentum of an object is defined as the product of its ____ and the angular velocity.
e: Angular momentum ($L$) is the rotational analog of linear momentum, calculated as $L = I\omega$.

q: For linear motion, the momentum is equal to the product of the ____ and the velocity.
e: Linear momentum ($p$) is defined as $p = mv$, where mass is the measure of inertia in linear motion.

q: The moment of inertia is analogous to mass and the angular velocity is analogous to the ____.
e: Rotational kinematic quantities have direct analogs in linear kinematics.

q: The formula for angular momentum is ____.
e: This equation defines angular momentum as the product of rotational inertia and rotational speed.

q: In SI units, since the unit of moment of inertia is $kg \cdot m^2$ and that of angular velocity is $rad \cdot s^{-1}$, the unit of angular momentum is ____.
e: Multiplying the units of moment of inertia and angular velocity yields the SI unit for angular momentum.

q: Angular momentum is a ____ quantity.
e: Angular momentum has both magnitude and a specific direction determined by the right-hand rule.

q: The law of ____ is also one fundamental law of physics.
e: This law states that angular momentum remains constant in the absence of external torques.

q: This law states that: If there is no ____ acting on an isolated system, the total angular momentum of the system is constant.
e: Just as linear momentum is conserved when net external force is zero, angular momentum is conserved when net external torque is zero.

q: In symbols, if $\Sigma \tau = 0$, then ____.
e: This is the mathematical representation of the conservation of angular momentum.

q: Her rate of spin (angular speed) increases greatly as her ____ decreases by pulling in her arms inwards.
e: By pulling her arms in, the skater reduces her moment of inertia, causing her angular velocity to increase to conserve angular momentum.

q: If she wants to slow down her rotation, she will stretch her arms ____.
e: Stretching arms outwards increases the moment of inertia, which correspondingly decreases the angular speed.

q: When her moment of inertia increases, the rotational angular speed will ____.
e: Angular speed and moment of inertia are inversely proportional when angular momentum is conserved.

q: An example of conservation of angular momentum is seen in an ____ performing a spin.
e: Ice skaters demonstrate this principle visibly by changing their body configuration to alter their spin rate.

q: A ____ who is rotating when jumping off the board does not need to make any physical effort to continue rotating.
e: Once in the air, the diver is an isolated system with negligible external torque, so their angular momentum is conserved.

q: The moment of inertia of a disc is given by the formula ____.
e: This is the standard moment of inertia for a uniform solid disc or cylinder rotating about its central axis.
